description: [A] H7 inline u64 keys (FxHashMap<u64>) for 1..=7-byte tokens: composite 1.458 [1.457,1.459]; ascii_prose 2.16x slower; cold start 1.75x

asi.hypothesis: H7 inline u64 keys (FxHashMap<u64>) for 1..=7-byte tokens
asi.learned: FxHash on u64 = key*SEED: low bits of the product depend only on low bits of the key, hashbrown indexes buckets by low bits, and 3-7 byte ASCII tokens share their first two bytes heavily -> long probe chains. Inline keys are not the problem; the integer hash is
asi.next_action_hint: H7b: same layout with a real 64-bit mixer (splitmix finalizer) as the hasher

description: [A] H7b inline u64 keys + splitmix64 hasher: composite 1.016 [1.014,1.018]; cjk/numeric -5% but ascii_prose/mixed +5.5%, whitespace +8%; cold start 1.6x (second 65k-entry table build)

asi.hypothesis: H7b inline u64 keys + splitmix64 hasher
asi.learned: inline keys do not beat FxHashMap<Vec<u8>> here: ascii_prose pieces mostly hit the whole-piece lookup once, where the Vec<u8> key compare on a 4-7 byte token is one cache line anyway; splitmix mixing costs ~3 multiplies vs Fx 1 per probe. Vocab build now populates two maps -> cold start regresses
asi.next_action_hint: attack lookup count instead of lookup cost: H4 count-only path, H6 output capacity, or skip the whole-piece hash for 1-2 byte pieces via tables (already), and avoid hashing in span_rank for 2-byte spans (already). Try B: avoid rank_of recomputation for final ids by caching ranks in parts

description: [A] H7c open-addressing inline-key table + tag bytes for 1..=7-byte tokens: composite 1.128 [1.124,1.133]; branch-miss 1.65->2.87%, cache-misses 2x vs FxHashMap<Vec<u8>>; code -2.5% only arm to gain

asi.hypothesis: H7c open-addressing inline-key table + tag bytes for 1..=7-byte tokens
asi.learned: three inline-key layouts (Fx u64, splitmix u64 via hashbrown, hand-rolled linear probing with tags) all lose to FxHashMap<Vec<u8>>. Root cause: most rank lookups in the merge loop are MISSES (candidate pairs not in vocab); hashbrown resolves a miss with one 16-byte SIMD group compare, linear probing at load 0.72 walks ~7 tag bytes with a mispredicting exit; at load 0.36 the 2 MB table falls out of L2. The whole-piece hit path is not the bottleneck
asi.rollback_reason: composite regression; 3rd consecutive discard at this hypothesis -> change altitude
asi.next_action_hint: C: SWAR ASCII scanner (piece_end+class_at = 32% of ascii_prose); B: output with_capacity; A: H5 cold start; later revisit lookup as a SWAR-group table if ever

description: [C] H9 SWAR 8-byte ASCII class-run scan: 13.68->12.80 (0.936 [0.933,0.938]); ascii_prose 0.835, code 0.907; cjk/mixed +0.6-0.8% within rule (first-word check cost on non-ASCII)

asi.hypothesis: H9 SWAR 8-byte ASCII class-run scan
asi.learned: SWAR eq() must be written as !((x^v)+0x7F) & HI; the sub-based form carries across lanes. Exhaustive per-lane test now guards it. One guard rework used.
asi.next: B: output Vec capacity / count-only path; A: H5 cold start (9.9 ms, base64 parse of 65k lines)

description: [B] H11 inline fixed-width key compare (TokenKey/Span, no memcmp): composite 1.043 [1.041,1.046]; ascii_prose 0.961 but cjk 1.121, short_strings 1.103

asi.hypothesis: H11 inline fixed-width key compare (TokenKey/Span, no memcmp)
asi.learned: replacing memcmp with 2 overlapping loads helps prose (4-8 B ASCII tokens) but the length-band match adds a mispredicting branch on CJK/whitespace runs where key lengths vary per probe; net loss. One unsafe block was needed (Path-style repr(transparent) cast) and is gone with the revert.
asi.next_action_hint: stop chasing the compare; reduce lookups: keep part ranks so the final windows() pass reuses the merge results (each merged span was just looked up)

description: [B] H12 carry token ranks through merge (no id-pass lookups): composite 0.994 [0.988,1.000] fails CI<1 and whitespace_heavy 1.089 [1.062,1.144] > 1.03; short_strings 0.961, cjk 0.982

asi.hypothesis: H12 carry token ranks through merge (no id-pass lookups)
asi.learned: saving the final windows() lookups (~1 per output token) is worth 2-4% on short/cjk but the extra 4-byte token field per part makes parts.remove and the min-scan slower on long whitespace runs. Reworks tried: pack Part to 8 bytes (u16 token, u8 start) -> whitespace +22% cycles (?), branch-free u64 min over (rank<<32|idx) -> +20% instructions everywhere; both worse.
asi.next_action_hint: whitespace_heavy is dominated by merge_scan on long runs (avg piece 7.5 B but 3258 pieces >16 B); consider lowering HEAP_THRESHOLD per class or a cheaper rescan (SoA ranks array so min-scan is a tight u32 loop)
